observations.detail: DEL does not call _is_expired before checking existence. An expired-but-not-yet-cleaned-up key would be treated as existent by DEL (returning OK instead of ERR key_not_found). However, this does not violate any MUST requirement, as M3's 'key does not exist' refers to keys genuinely never stored / already deleted. The SHOULD S4 specifies expired keys SHOULD be treated as non-existent, and the practical impact is minimal since _is_expired cleanup is triggered by GET/EXISTS/KEYS/COUNT calls.

Command parsing is case-insensitive (tokens[0].upper()), and SET values support spaces via ' '.join(args[1:]). Keys are single-token (no quoted-key support), consistent with the simple text protocol design.
All 15 existing tests in tests/test_protocol.py pass per executor1 report. Tests cover: M1, M2, M3, M4, M5, M6, M7, M9, M10, M11, M12(x2), S5.
